Hi Samir —

Appreciate the context and the timeline. See attached: our current DPA template (Redwood_DPA_Template_v2.docx). High-level answers to your two asks:

- Transfers: We default to the EU SCCs for controller-to-processor transfers; when customers want, we can also rely on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework where applicable — we can confirm per-tenant.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a public list of subprocessors and publish updates on a rolling basis; for contract purposes we typically: (a) commit to notify customers of additions 30 days in advance, and (b) allow customers to object on reasonable privacy/security grounds. We don't disclose vendor-level SOC reports automatically, but we can provide attestations and, in limited cases, redacted evidence under NDA.

A couple of quick clarifying questions for NovaTech so we can get ahead of redlines:
- Do you need a full infra-level disclosure (including CDNs and cloud infra partners), or just subprocessors that process customer content/data?
- Is a 30-day notice window acceptable, or do you need prior approval for any new subprocessor?

If you prefer, Marissa (cc'd) can propose limited redlines to accelerate execution; otherwise we can exchange edits and move to DocuSign.

Best,

Subject: RNW proposed redlines for NovaTech DPA (internal)

Olga / Karthik —

Drafted a short set of comment-level redlines to keep NovaTech comfortable while protecting platform ops. Key points:

- Transfer mechanism: keep SCCs as default; agree to Data Privacy Framework only where customer requires it and it's technically appropriate.
- Subprocessor notice: propose 30-day notice + a limited objection right (customer can request mitigation or alternative services but cannot unreasonably block).
- Audit right: suggest limiting full on-site audits to escalations; default to remote evidence (certification copies, SOC summaries). On-site or deep-dive audits would require scoped approval and could incur cost recovery.
- Liability/indemnity: no unlimited indemnity; cap at fees paid in 12 months except for willful misconduct / breach of security obligations.

I've attached the redlines and a short exec memo describing risks if we concede broader audit or approval rights. If we need speed, I can prepare a DocuSign-ready version with tracked changes removed.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
